advice: A useful n=512 specialization is to keep the existing four-tile SME transpose and arithmetic, but remove repeated tail handling from that path. Add a compile-time n=512 variant with fixed bounds and all-active predicates, selected only when n == 512; retain the current general kernel for every other n and for n <= 0. The supplied source already shows the necessary four-tile layout and full-tile outer-product operations. At n=512, its tiles are full when the runtime streaming vector length divides 512 into complete 2VL blocks; verify that condition before using all-active loads or stores. Keep accumulation in FP32 and preserve increasing-k order. This is a candidate optimization, not a measured gain.
risks: The evidence does not establish the streaming vector length or that 512 always forms complete tiles on the target, so an unchecked all-active specialization could access past array bounds. Fixed bounds may also be optimized identically to the existing loops, giving no speedup. Do not attribute any future joint result to this change alone without isolated paired controls.
